research.text: My research brings together medical imaging AI, quantitative biomarkers and clinical evaluation. I work across structural and diffusion MRI and thoracic CT, connecting methodological development with questions in diagnosis, disease characterisation and clinical translation.

My research develops MRI and machine learning methods to identify and delineate subtle brain abnormalities associated with focal epilepsy, particularly focal cortical dysplasia. This includes unsupervised lesion detection using ultra-high-field 7T MRI and multimodal segmentation using T1-weighted and FLAIR images. I focus on detecting small lesions, understanding model failures and evaluating performance across imaging settings.
Predicting seizure recurrence after a first seizure

A first unprovoked seizure raises an important clinical question: will another seizure occur? My research investigates whether structural MRI, combined with clinical information, can help estimate this risk. Through NeuroMorphix, I study brain asymmetry and other imaging features, with evaluation in an independent patient cohort to assess how well predictions generalise.

My research investigates how structural MRI can characterise brain changes across normal cognition, mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer’s disease. Using cortical and subcortical measurements, I examine regional anatomical differences and networks that describe similarities between brain regions. This work combines machine learning with harmonisation across imaging sites to evaluate potential biomarkers for distinguishing clinical groups.
Friedreich’s ataxia: diffusion MRI and cerebellar pathways

My research uses diffusion MRI and deep learning to study the cerebellar pathways affected by Friedreich’s ataxia. I develop automated methods to segment the cerebellar peduncles and extract quantitative measurements of white matter microstructure. The work evaluates segmentation accuracy and consistency across imaging sites, with the aim of supporting reproducible imaging biomarkers of neurological disease.

At I-MED Radiology Network, I lead research delivery and analysis in occupational lung imaging. ExactDust examines agreement and diagnostic performance between chest radiography and HRCT. Related work focuses on quantitative HRCT assessment of structural lung abnormalities.
My ACARP-supported research evaluates CT-derived measures of lung function against spirometry and other available pulmonary function measures in coal mine dust lung disease.

Across these projects, I focus on validation in clinical cohorts, multi-site variability, harmonisation, error analysis and transparent reporting. My experience spans clinical data curation, imaging quality control, segmentation, statistical analysis and reproducible machine learning pipelines.
Methods: MRI and CT analysis · Deep learning · Quantitative biomarkers · Multi-site harmonisation · Diagnostic performance evaluation

about.text: I am a medical imaging AI researcher based in Brisbane, Australia. My work combines machine learning, structural and diffusion MRI, and quantitative CT to investigate neurological and occupational lung disease. I am particularly interested in how robust image analysis and careful clinical evaluation can turn imaging measurements into useful evidence.

Senior Researcher · I-MED Radiology Network
Clinical AI evaluation, quantitative imaging and occupational lung disease research.

Honorary Fellow · The University of Queensland
Neuroimaging and medical imaging AI research.

Adjunct Lecturer · Charles Darwin University
Appointed September 2026.

I completed my PhD in machine learning and neuroimaging at The University of Queensland in 2024, supervised by Professor David Reutens and Associate Professor Viktor Vegh. My doctoral research focused on MRI and machine learning in epilepsy.

My previous research appointments include QIMR Berghofer’s Cerebellum & Neurodegeneration Research Group, UQ’s Centre for Advanced Imaging, and a visiting research role with RBWH Neurology. Earlier research experience at IIIT Sri City and the University of Hyderabad established my foundations in machine learning and feature selection.
Education: PhD, The University of Queensland (2024); M.Tech in Information Technology, University of Hyderabad (2016); MCA (2013) and BCA (2010), West Bengal University of Technology.
PReMI–Springer Student Award (2017) · MICCAI Student Participation Award (2021) · UQ HDR travel support to attend AES (2023).
Academic service includes reviewing for ML4H and programme committee contributions to the ICCV CVAMD workshop.
For a current academic CV, collaboration enquiries or supervision discussions, contact soumen.ghosh@uq.edu.au.

teaching.text: I teach across machine learning, data science and mathematical foundations, and supervise student research in medical image analysis. My approach connects conceptual understanding with reproducible experiments, careful evaluation and clear scientific communication.

I supervise postgraduate and undergraduate research projects in medical imaging AI. Current supervision includes B.Tech Computer Science students developing a shared brain MRI lesion segmentation pipeline.
Projects emphasise data quality, preprocessing, reproducible training, meaningful baselines, lesion-level evaluation and failure analysis.

Brain MRI lesion detection and segmentation

Structural and diffusion MRI biomarkers

Quantitative thoracic imaging

Robustness and clinical evaluation of imaging AI
